title: Agent autonomy/security evaluations and incidents/near-misses
ranking_basis: Inspectable task metadata; official revision/mechanism evidence; organizer defensive contest corrections.
interpretation_guards: Source families, datasets, events, artifacts, experiments and observation versions are separate units.
No pooled risk, universal autonomy score, causal harm rate or p(doom) conversion.
No attack instructions, conversation/injection/tool-argument payloads, account identifiers, personal names, biometric or patient details.
Archive version never substitutes for historical runtime version. Unknown cost,budget,assistance and timestamps remain null.
Rights and actual audit-log access remain held when not explicitly established.

collections.name: AgentDojo task-level evaluation metadata
collections.historical_coverage: Dated 2024–2025 results; one clean archive file introduced June 4, 2024. Introduction is not runtime time.
collections.update_frequency: Research additions and corrections; no fixed cadence.
collections.access_export: One existing clean JSON privately checked; public synthetic-only offline decoder. No attacked trace acquisition.
collections.measurement_regime: Short task-level utility and attack-condition outcomes with separate runtime metadata.
collections.author_authority: Benchmark maintainers; publisher scoring predicates, not independent operational security assessment.
limitations: Clean security=True is a default, not resistance. Targeted-goal success and DoS nonutility predicates differ; error paths can assign flags without observed outcomes.
Archive and sample-introduction code are not a certified runtime revision. All actual attacked results remain uninterpreted in v0.
Short banking tasks do not establish multi-hour reliability. Heterogeneous published combinations are not a fair complete leaderboard.
Software/documentation MIT does not establish generated conversation or third-party trace rights. Raw payloads remain excluded.

overlap_review.current_scope: One original combined intake item 13, seven collections; not split into two original receipts.

per_catalog_review.review: AP002 has the same METR producer but distinct randomized real-work productivity studies. No time-horizon task/run match is established; actual developer duration, survey predictions and horizon human baseline cannot be merged.

AE004 shares OpenAI as producer but concerns 2020 efficiency research, not 2025 sycophancy. AE001 defensive benchmark analogies do not create common experiments. No item 13 artifact/run/event identity found.
Safety-evaluation theme and overlapping model labels do not identify AgentDojo or tau runs. No item 13 family/artifact/run identity found; no nationality-based risk inference.
CD001 deployment disclosure metadata is a different collection and jurisdiction from NHTSA/OAIC. Organization/provider references are not incident or causal links.
Historical benchmark artifacts and shared model/task terminology are distinct evaluation families. No item 13 benchmark version, run or event identity found.
Human-AI interaction and feedback studies are distinct controlled study cohorts. They do not constitute independent clinical-harm evidence for the sycophancy incident.
Model metadata and availability references do not establish same evaluations, scaffolds or outcomes. No item 13 family/artifact identity found.

OS004 is already GL014 OpenAI governance/deployment enrichment. Sycophancy pair adds a new incident/postmortem subtype, not a new producer family. OS002 METR external automated-R&D review is a different assessment; its report revisions must not be mistaken for horizon revisions.
PI001/PI002/PI005 use LLMs in controlled studies; shared GPT labels do not join participants, treatments, events or harm. No sycophancy event identity found.

BARN/RoboArena/TriFinger/PhAIL/STRANDS are evaluation/deployment evidence families distinct from NHTSA roadway reports and Cruise recall. Physical failures/interventions are not the same road incident/exposure regime.

SP003 is METR RE-Bench enrichment of GL004 and references the same mutable eval-analysis-public README. This is documentation overlap, not verified identical README bytes, task membership or run observations. RE-Bench best-of-k allocated budgets differ from horizon success-vs-human-time regression.
Data provenance/synthetic feedback studies are not evidence that feedback or memory caused the OpenAI deployment regression. No common experiment/event identity found.

corrections.correction: AgentDojo security=True is not safety: clean default, error assignments, targeted goal and DoS semantics remain distinct.
Historical source at sample introduction corroborates predicates without proving actual runtime; real attacked outcomes remain uninterpreted.
Root software MIT does not clear generated trace rights; only synthetic fixtures are public.
AIxCC 70 to 63 denominator correction is one revision; 68%-of-identified prose conflicts with 43/54.
AIxCC reported USD 152 and 45 minutes are aggregates, not actual task budgets or caps.
tau pass^k is all-trial reliability, not pass@k; later airline results do not inherit original retail costs.
METR FAQ 137 minutes differs from current TH1.1 203.012577 and TH1.0 130.816528; human time is not runtime.
METR suite/infrastructure changes, estimated long baselines, regularization correction and six/eight-run wording are version-scoped.
NHTSA affected equipment, submitted manufacturer mechanisms and agency processing corrections do not establish victim counts or independent causality.
OAIC original determination date differs from announcement; ART partly reverses findings and later regulator statements update status.
OAIC 63/62 stores and February/March review wording remain source-dated discrepancies.
Two OpenAI postmortems represent one incident; operator explanation is not controlled causal or clinical-harm evidence.
Five new families and two enrichments remain unadmitted; source-family absence is not event-level absence from incident indexes.
